target_pattern: Narrate past events by combining imperfect for background/habit and preterite for completed events, including meaning shifts in verbs like poder, querer, saber, and conocer.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Using one generic past tense for every situation.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Spanish past narration usually combines two layers: imperfect for context or ongoing action, and preterite for completed events that move the story forward.
target_pattern_formula: Imperfecto for repeated or habitual past (siempre, de niño, todos los días)
Pretérito for finished actions with clear endpoint (ayer, anoche, de repente)
natural_examples: Estaba en casa cuando sonó el teléfono.
Cuando era niño, iba al parque todos los sábados.
Mientras trabajaba, recibí un mensaje urgente.
Había mucho tráfico cuando salí de casa.

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as directed.
drills: Base: Estaba en casa cuando sonó el teléfono. -> change casa to oficina.
Base: Cuando era niño, iba al parque. -> change to plural nosotros.
Base: Quería salir, pero no podía. -> change to successful completion with preterite.
Base: Conocía a Marta desde 2018. -> change to I met Marta in 2018.
Base: Sabía la respuesta. -> change to I found out the answer yesterday.
Base: Mientras trabajaba, escuché un ruido. -> make it a question.
Base: Había mucho tráfico cuando salí. -> change salí to salimos.
Base: Jugábamos tenis los domingos. -> make it negative.
Base: Estuve leyendo dos horas. -> change to I was reading when you called me.
Base: No quise responder. -> change to ongoing desire (imperfect).
Base: Podía levantar la caja. -> change to I managed to lift the box.
Base: El cielo parecía gris. -> add and it started to rain.
Base: Dijo que conocía a Juan. -> change to She said she met Juan.
Base: Cuando llegué, todos bailaban. -> change bailaban to completed action.
Base: Íbamos al gimnasio los lunes. -> change time frame to el lunes pasado.

contrastive_discrimination.instructions: Choose the best option in Spanish based on meaning.
prompts: I could finish it (and I did). (podía vs pude)
I was able to finish it in general, but maybe I did not. (podía vs pude)
I met Ana in 2020. (conocía vs conocí)
I knew Ana when we worked together. (conocía vs conocí)
I found out yesterday. (sabía vs supe)
I did not know your number. (no sabía vs no supe)
I refused to go. (no quería vs no quise)
I wanted to go (ongoing feeling). (quería vs quise)
We were talking when he arrived. (hablamos vs hablábamos)
Yesterday we talked for ten minutes. (hablamos vs hablábamos)

guided_personal_writing.instructions: Write one Spanish sentence for each specific meaning.
prompts: You were working when someone important called you.
When you were younger, you used to study at night.
You wanted to rest yesterday, but you could not.
You found out important news this morning.
You met a new person at work last month.
You already knew that person from before.
There was a lot of noise while you were in a meeting.
You were reading when your phone rang.
Your team used to meet every Friday.
Yesterday your team met only once.
It looked like it was going to rain, and then it rained.
You refused to sign something because it was unclear.
You could complete a difficult task after several attempts.
When you arrived home, everyone was already eating.
For many years you worked in a specific field.

prompts_en: I was in the middle of cooking when he showed up.
I found out too late.
I wanted to explain it, but he refused to listen.
Back then, we used to see each other every week.
I could do it yesterday, and I did it.
At that moment, it looked like a bad idea.
When I got there, they were already leaving.
I met her at a conference, but I already knew her company.
There was traffic, so I arrived late.
I was reading for three hours before deciding.

common_errors.mistake: Using only preterite for all past narration
common_errors.why_it_happens: English simple past covers many uses that Spanish splits into two tenses.

common_errors.mistake: Using imperfect for one-time completed actions
common_errors.why_it_happens: Learners over-associate past description with imperfect.
Ignoring special preterite meaning of no quise.
English uses knew in broader ways.
Word-for-word transfer from English timing logic.
Accent marks are often dropped in fast writing.

common_errors.mistake: Estaba leyendo dos horas for completed duration
common_errors.why_it_happens: Overusing imperfect continuous in duration contexts.

common_errors.mistake: Mixed person endings in same sentence
common_errors.why_it_happens: Focus on tense but not subject agreement.
